title: BPD Test
description: See how often you experience shifting emotions, fear of rejection, and impulsivity.

questions.bpd_1: I have an extreme fear that the people I love will leave me.
questions.bpd_2: My feelings toward people close to me often swing drastically from adoring them to hating them.
questions.bpd_3: I often feel hollow or emotionally empty inside.
questions.bpd_4: I often doubt who I really am or what my purpose in life is.
questions.bpd_5: I act impulsively when I'm sad or angry (e.g. overspending, overeating, risky things).
questions.bpd_6: I have thought about or acted on hurting myself when I felt extremely distressed.
questions.bpd_7: My mood can change very drastically within hours or even minutes.
questions.bpd_8: I often feel so angry that it's hard to control.
questions.bpd_9: Under heavy stress, I feel detached from my body or feel like the world isn't real (dissociation).
questions.bpd_10: When I'm anxious, I often accuse others of having bad intentions toward me.
questions.bpd_11: I find it hard to keep friendships or romantic relationships stable.
questions.bpd_12: I often feel that no one truly understands or cares about me.
questions.bpd_13: My sadness feels far more intense and painful than it does for most people.
questions.bpd_14: I often need constant reassurance and attention to feel safe.
questions.bpd_15: When someone cancels plans, I feel completely crushed or betrayed.
questions.bpd_16: I tend to do whatever it takes (begging, threatening) so people won't leave me.
questions.bpd_17: I'm very reactive and easily hurt by even the smallest criticism.
questions.bpd_18: I often feel bored and look for risky thrills to make the boredom go away.
questions.bpd_19: I often let out anger by shouting, swearing, or breaking things.
questions.bpd_20: When I feel lonely, I feel like my existence in this world is meaningless.

results.description: Your emotions are stable and you have a healthy view of relationships.
You sometimes experience emotional instability or a fear of abandonment that gets in the way.
Many of your symptoms line up with borderline criteria. Talking to a psychologist is strongly recommended.
